newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark breaks prop, new target 1.69.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark breaks prop, new target 1.69.

text.p: The dollar broke below a tough band of resistance at 1.70/6980 marks on Monday, setting sights on a new downside target of 1.69 marks, technical analysts said on Monday.
Only four trading sessions after posting a three-year high at 1.7375 marks, the dollar fell through layers of resistance to hit a low of 1.6967 shortly after the U.S. midday.
The dollar struggled earlier to break the 1.70/6980 level, a psychological barrier and a 50 percent retracement of the dollar's previous April rise from 1.6615 to 1.7375 marks.

"We could move lower to test 1.69 marks, which would be a 62 percent retracement of the recent rise and also a bull trendline which dates back to December 31," said Scott Siller, senior technical analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch.
However, most technicians were dubious of a prolonged sell-off, with few expecting dollar/mark to topple the 1.69 prop.

"The decline we've seen over the past week or so is more finished than not," said Darren Spain, a technical analyst at Credit Suisse in New York. "(A move below 1.70/6980) presents another opportunity to buy."
Another chartist at a U.S. investment bank said dollar/mark would not break the 1.69 support.
"I don't want to get on that bandwagon. I just don't see another big move down," the technician said.

Technicians could not ignore fundamentals as the French franc fell to its lowest level against the mark in more than a month on news President Jacques Chirac was poised to call a snap parliamentary election nine months ahead of schedule in a broadcast to the nation on Monday.

Other European currencies were dragged down against the mark as the possibility of France's power passing into the hands of a Socialist-led alliance made markets fear that France, a core candidate for European monetary union, may have difficulty balancing pro-EMU policies with efforts for economic growth.

Technicians said mark gains should peak at 3.38 French francs. Mark/Paris hit a high of 3.3772 on Monday after ending European trade at 3.3694/99 on Friday. The mark also posted solid gains against the yen.
"What's keeping the pressure on dollar/mark is this nice upmove in mark versus yen and...most of Europe," Siller said.
Meanwhile, dollar/yen held within its five-day 125 to 126.18 range.
"Any approach to 125 the figure is a very good buying opportunity," Spain said. "We have good support and the market has noted Japanese buy interest down there."
